evidence.cheapest_resolving_test: Show a one-page control prototype to ten Polish or EU product, compliance, and agency leads, ask them to map one live workflow and its accountable party, then request a paid fixed-scope pilot without claiming legal certification.
evidence.proposition: From 2 August 2026 the AI Office and national authorities begin enforcement, while specified interactive AI and generated or altered content face disclosure, labelling, and machine-readable marking requirements.

evidence.cheapest_resolving_test: Interview five refrigerant or equipment importers and five HVAC or refrigeration contractors in Poland using screenshots of their present label, report, certificate, and portal workflows, then seek one prepaid narrowly scoped cleanup or submission engagement.
evidence.proposition: EU implementing rules under Regulation 2024/573 changed F-gas label and annual-report formats, expanded mandatory technician certification to equipment using alternatives, and specified registration controls for the F-gas Portal.

evidence.cheapest_resolving_test: Show one-page fixed-scope offers to 15 named operators in each niche and seek three paid deposits contingent on a documented applicability screen.
evidence.proposition: An official 2025 sector report describes expanding EU cyber obligations, including supply-chain security, incident reporting, product-lifecycle vulnerability management, and likely demand for audits, testing, consulting, and certification among Polish SMEs and suppliers to regulated entities.

evidence.cheapest_resolving_test: Interview ten municipal social-care directors and five contracted providers using the audit findings, then request two paid, eight-week pilots with predefined administrative-hours or missed-visit outcomes.
evidence.proposition: Poland's Supreme Audit Office reports weak identification of at-risk seniors, imprecise care-service records, missing quality monitoring, funding interruptions, specialist shortages, and absence of basic home care in some rural and mixed municipalities.

evidence.cheapest_resolving_test: Interview five Polish employment-law or payroll partners using a one-page mock deliverable, then seek one paid fixed-scope data-mapping pilot from an employer with at least 100 staff while counsel verifies the applicable Polish text.
evidence.proposition: The European Commission states that new EU pay-transparency rules require salary-range disclosure, employee access to individual and sex-disaggregated peer pay information, gender-pay-gap publication by employers with at least 100 employees, and an assessment when an unjustified gap of at least 5% appears; compensation, penalties, representation, and a shifted burden of proof create concrete loss events.

evidence.cheapest_resolving_test: Run a tabletop incident with five EU hardware or embedded-software manufacturers, timing awareness-to-draft handoffs, and ask for a paid setup only where the existing process misses ownership or deadline evidence.
evidence.proposition: The European Commission states that from 11 September 2026 manufacturers of products with digital elements must report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents, with an early warning within 24 hours, fuller notification within 72 hours, later final reports, and a single submission through the ENISA reporting platform.

evidence.cheapest_resolving_test: Show one-page paid offers to three metal firms, three industrial heat users, and three renewable developers, and ask each for a conditional letter of intent tied to a named live transaction.
evidence.proposition: The Commission reports active EU mechanisms around industrial decarbonisation, including counter-guarantees for clean-energy PPAs, an industrial process-heat auction, grid and flexibility measures, priority sustainability requirements for steel and aluminium, and public monitoring of metal scrap flows.

evidence.cheapest_resolving_test: With one consenting owner in each target category, request export or third-party delivery from three equipment brands and attempt one decision-grade report before building software.
evidence.proposition: The EU Data Act applies and gives consumers and businesses access to and sharing rights over raw data from connected products, explicitly including cars and industrial machinery and pointing to repair, maintenance, manufacturing, and agriculture uses.

evidence.cheapest_resolving_test: Interview ten Polish SME finance owners with overdue invoices and ask each to submit one real invoice to a manual paid pilot with an explicit fee or success charge.
evidence.proposition: The European Commission reports that late payments remain widespread, payment periods exceed sixty days on average in both business and government transactions, larger firms are less likely to pay on time, and collection imposes administrative burden; this supports testing supplier-side products that reduce delay, uncertainty, and collection effort.

evidence.cheapest_resolving_test: Offer a manual document-and-registry verification on twenty live heat-pump quotes through two installers and measure whether households, installers, importers, or lenders pay for the report.
evidence.proposition: Polish authorities found documentation, labeling, and declaration problems in most inspected non-EU heat-pump models and state that missing records deprive buyers of information and evidence needed to judge compliance and safety; this supports testing independent verification and accountability services.
